observation.visible_scene: A wide beach view at sunset/sunrise: a layered sky of orange, yellow and teal clouds above a glowing horizon, a band of ocean with a line of breaking white foam in the middle, and a foreground of wet, mirror-like sand reflecting the warm sky colors. A thin dark diagonal channel/crack runs across the wet sand.
visible_changes: The white foam line of the breaking wave continuously reshapes and shifts slightly in thickness and vertical position across the segment, indicating the surf is mid-cycle (already advancing and receding at the start, not beginning or ending).
The thin sheet of water on the wet sand and its orange/teal reflections shimmer and change subtly frame to frame.
The dark diagonal line on the sand stays in the same position throughout, marking it as a static surface feature rather than a moving object.
The cloud shapes and the bright sun-glow at the horizon remain essentially unchanged over the ~2.7 s, showing no large-scale sky motion within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the visible wave will crest, break fully, or drain back out after the last frame.
Any longer-term drift of the clouds or fading of the sunset beyond this short crop.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is not clearly evidenced: the frame edges and horizon stay aligned, so the shot appears static or nearly so, but a very slight drift cannot be ruled out.
The exact phase of the wave (advancing vs. receding) is hard to pin down because the foam line changes shape rather than translating cleanly.
